req.title: Reject wrong method on /delete
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than DELETE on /delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /delete must respond with HTTP 405 for any method other than DELETE. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/POST/PUT/PATCH return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the full set of common HTTP methods to ensure the method-whitelist is exactly {DELETE} and not a superset. Each test asserts exact status codes to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_method_returns_200():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

tests.name: test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH requests to /delete
Verify DELETE returns exactly 200 (boundary: the one allowed method)
expected: DELETE -> 200 (the boundary between allowed and disallowed)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: Boundary between allowed method (DELETE=200) and all others (405)
BVA: exactly one method is allowed; all adjacent methods in the set must be rejected
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405():
    disallowed = [
        ('GET', client.get('/delete')),
        ('POST', client.post('/delete')),
        ('PUT', client.put('/delete')),
        ('PATCH', client.patch('/delete')),
    ]
    for method_name, r in disallowed:
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"{method_name} expected 405, got {r.status_code}"
    allowed = client.delete('/delete')
    assert allowed.status_code == 200

test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_payload_structure():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert data['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert 'form' in data
    assert 'data' in data
    assert 'files' in data
    assert 'json' in data

test_delete_response_payload_structure()
